page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.48xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.7 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps. There is no local NVMe storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

In multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks, the m8gb.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance. Multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation via Clang all rank in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 21,353.49 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 483.46 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. LLM inference prompt processing for small models is relatively weak, though medium model prompt processing achieves average speeds.

Given its high physical core density and top-tier multi-core efficiency, the instance offers strong qualitative cost-of-resource efficiency for highly parallelized workloads. The lack of local storage means workloads requiring high-speed local disk I/O must rely on network-attached storage, which is supported by the 200 Gbps network interface. The server is highly suited for large-scale database operations, high-throughput static web serving, Redis key-value stores, and multi-threaded data processing.
